Floating UI traps

Five page behaviours that break an overlay. With the extension off every section must still trap. With QA mode on, every pass line below must hold.

1. Focus-trapped modal

A plain div modal wired like a focus scope: a bubble-phase focusin on the document pulls focus back whenever it lands outside, and Escape on document capture closes the modal.

Pass: picking #modal-input and typing into the comment box leaves refocused at 0 and the modal open, and Escape closes QA mode rather than the modal.

2. Dropdown dismissed on outside pointerdown

While the dropdown is open, a bubble-phase pointerdown on the document closes it as soon as the pointer goes down anywhere outside it.

Pass: clicking an item inside the dropdown to pick it leaves the dropdown open, and the item is in the screenshot.

3. Hover tooltip with a grace area

Two closers, both real: a pointerout handler on the trigger, and a document pointermove that hides the tooltip once the pointer is more than 40px outside the trigger box.

Tooltip content that has to survive being annotated.

Pass: moving the pointer over the trigger and then over the tooltip leaves the tooltip visible, and the tooltip is in the screenshot.

4. Native modal

A real <dialog> opened with showModal(), so it sits in the browser top layer where z-index alone loses to it.

Pass: with the dialog open the overlay paints above it, but nothing in the overlay can be clicked or focused, because the browser makes everything outside a modal dialog inert. Escape still turns QA mode off. Close the dialog to annotate.

5. Type-to-focus composer

A composer that grabs any keystroke landing elsewhere, either from a bubble-phase document listener or from a capture-phase window listener. Capture is the hard case.

Pass: with thief mode at capture, typing a comment leaves every character in the comment box and the composer empty. stolen may climb, the thief just does not get the last word.
